raw_llm_translation: A visitor brings blessings. (A visitor brings food)

og_rag_translation: The one who despises the calf will not own a cow.
traditional_rag_translation: You don't appreciate the value of a cow until you lose it.
raw_llm_translation: You don't show a grown-up how a cow is roped.
expert_translation: Generosity ruins the man who gives his cows to morning visitors.

og_rag_translation: A home without a heart is not a home (A hollow gourd makes no sound)
traditional_rag_translation: There is no heart in a stomach (A big stomach doesn't have a heart).
raw_llm_translation: The stomach is not a sack (A big stomach doesn't mean a big heart).
expert_translation: He who has nothing has no heart.
cultural_context: [Kikuyu proverb on wealth, entrepreneurship, and traditional wisdom]

og_rag_translation: One does not inherit poverty.
traditional_rag_translation: A place is not deserted without reason.
raw_llm_translation: A place you have never been to is called a wilderness.
expert_translation: A poor man is not invited to a private discussion.
cultural_context: [Kikuyu proverb on wealth, entrepreneurship, and traditional wisdom]

kikuyu_proverb: Utari ni wa kwa mari. (Muthiini egiritagia itonga) .
og_rag_translation: No one is born with wealth. (The morning sun does not promise riches).
traditional_rag_translation: He who is not at home does not inherit. (The absent one does not participate in the division of property).
raw_llm_translation: A poor man does not rule. (He who lacks counsel cannot lead).
expert_translation: A poor man leans on the rich. Kiswahili : Maskini hutegemea matajiri. Meaning: Each person needs another, regardless of status. Teaching: This proverb teaches that within a family or community, people cannot be equal. Some are poor and others rich. But they need each other for daily objectives to be achieved. Bible parallel: 1 Thessalonians 5:11 “Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.”
cultural_context: [Kikuyu proverb on wealth, entrepreneurship, and traditional wisdom]

og_rag_translation: The poor are not consulted.
traditional_rag_translation: Soil is not sold.
raw_llm_translation: A cooking pot is not ridiculed.
expert_translation: Beauty is not consumed.
cultural_context: [Kikuyu proverb on wealth, entrepreneurship, and traditional wisdom]

og_rag_translation: A man's wealth is his character.

og_rag_translation: The path to wealth is not walked in a day.

og_rag_translation: Wealth is like a bird.

raw_llm_translation: The poverty of a wise man is not obvious, it is his own secret.

og_rag_translation: Borrowed robes do not keep one warm.

og_rag_translation: Borrowers do not form a council.
